## Industry Problem

<!--
  instructor: Ask the room "why can't the agent just answer this?" before
  explaining — let someone land on "it doesn't know what's in the
  warehouse today" themselves. Ties directly back to 1_1: a plain LLM call
  has no way to reach outside its own training data.
-->

A retail company's support agent gets asked constantly: *"Do you have the blue medium hoodie in stock?"* A plain LLM cannot answer this — it has no idea what is in the warehouse today. Someone has to give the agent a way to actually look it up.

## Instructor / example demonstration

<!--
  instructor: Live-type this, don't paste it finished — the teaching moment
  is watching the docstring get written and asking "how would the model
  know when to call this?" before running anything. Explicitly point at the
  type hints and say they define the input schema, not just documentation.
  Prereq: only needs 1_1's environment setup.
-->

Here's the fix: turn the lookup into a tool the model can call, using LangChain's `@tool` decorator.

```python
from langchain.tools import tool

@tool
def check_inventory(sku: str) -> str:
    """Look up current stock count for a product SKU.

    Args:
        sku: The product's stock-keeping unit code, e.g. 'HOOD-BLU-M'
    """
    fake_warehouse = {"HOOD-BLU-M": 14, "HOOD-BLU-L": 0, "TEE-RED-S": 42}
    if sku not in fake_warehouse:
        return f"No record of SKU '{sku}'."
    return f"{fake_warehouse[sku]} unit(s) of '{sku}' in stock."
```

Notice the model never sees the function body — only the docstring, which is what it reads to decide *when* to call this tool at all.

## Run It Yourself

<!--
  instructor: ~10 min. Circulate for the most common snag: calling
  `check_inventory("HOOD-BLU-M")` instead of `.invoke({"sku": "HOOD-BLU-M"})`
  — the dict-argument convention trips people up every time, worth a
  reminder mid-activity rather than waiting for it to surface. Confirm
  everyone sees the tool run stand-alone before letting them wire up an agent.
-->

Paste the tool above into Colab and confirm it works stand-alone before trusting an agent with it:

```python
print(check_inventory.invoke({"sku": "HOOD-BLU-M"}))
print(check_inventory.invoke({"sku": "HOOD-BLU-L"}))
print(check_inventory.invoke({"sku": "GHOST-SKU"}))
```

Then wire it into a `create_agent` call (per [Tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools)) and ask a question that should trigger it: *"Is the blue medium hoodie in stock?"*

## Modify It, Build It

<!--
  instructor: ~15 min, pairs. Good work looks like a docstring specific
  enough that a partner can guess what the tool does and when the agent
  would call it, without reading the code. That guessing check is the
  actual assessment moment here — don't skip having partners do it out loud.
-->

Pick a different retail question your tool doesn't answer yet — *"When will the blue large hoodie be restocked?"* works well — and build a second custom tool for it. (Stretch goal: define its input with a Pydantic `args_schema` instead of plain type hints.) Have your partner read only the docstring and guess what the tool does.
